parent_models.justification: The distributed lag model is a type of dynamic linear model where the response at a given time depends linearly on current and past values of an input sequence.
Distributed lag models are part of state-based models because they consider the state (past information) to predict future behavior.
These models can be related if the lag structure is modeled to have memoryless properties akin to Markov processes.

closest_parent_model.justification: The 'dynamic linear model' is closest to the 'distributed lag model,' as both are fundamentally concerned with understanding dynamics in sequences and rely on linear relationships over time.
